links.outcome: Shift in medication-versus-self-care balance of depression advice under inference-time activation steering
links.effect: Medication-versus-self-care balance declined 0.32 per unit of steering amplitude (95% CI, -0.39 to -0.25; P<.001); largest shift (β=-0.44) in scenarios with no stated treatment preference; clinician referral unchanged (P=.63).
links.quote: Across 372 generations, steering produced a graded, dose-dependent shift in the medication-versus-self-care balance, which declined by 0.32 per unit of amplitude (β = −0.32; 95% CI, −0.39 to −0.25; P < .001); medication extent fell and self-care extent rose.

unlisted_practices: Disclosure standards for inference-time model modifications such as activation steering
Independent auditing of deployed LLMs for silent manipulation of treatment recommendations

screen.reason: Empirical study investigating model vulnerability/manipulability (inference-time activation steering) in mental health treatment recommendations, highlighting safety concerns rather than testing an organizational deployment safeguard.
